post.originalText:
Tested BRAG with Opus 5.5 👀

Used /brag-slim on Entune’s code to create this launch video. Really impressed with the result.

BRAG: https://t.co/XQFFTqzFFy

    Corrections that consider the context

    A match is not always a replacement.

    
      
        After transcription, when a dictionary match could mean your term or an everyday word, a decision model reads the words around it and applies only the meaning that fits. It chooses from your own entries. It never generates or rewrites your text.

          OpenAIOpenAI's Decisions API. The context goes to OpenAI, on your own API key.

          PerplexityCaught the most fixes in our test. The context goes to Perplexity, on your own API key.

          LayaRuns on your computer, in English, after a one-time install.

          Dictionary learned from 7.5 hours of the maintainer's dictation, transcribed by Parakeet, with entries suggested by GPT-6 Astra on a ChatGPT plan.

          Tested on the next 2.1 hours it had never seen: 160 recordings.

          Expected answers written down before any model ran. Jev, OpenAI and Laya were tested on October 7; Perplexity on October 8 with the same transcripts, dictionary and expected answers.

          One speaker, one reviewer judging from text, one run per model.

Each bar is a share of its own total: fixes out of the 47 places that should change, wrong swaps out of the 72 that should stay. These results do not establish a statistical ranking, including between 1 and 3 wrong swaps, or measure overall transcription accuracy.

          In the separate formatting test, of 92 places judged to need a paragraph or bullet, Jev placed 35 with 12 unwanted, Perplexity 32 with 5, OpenAI 8 with 1, and Laya 5 with 37.

    Your models

    Three jobs. You choose the model for each.

    Entune is free and MIT licensed, with no Entune subscription. Local speech models run on your computer without an API key or per-minute payment. Cloud speech, cloud decision models and dictionary generation use your own accounts and can cost money.

    Choosing models, in full →

  




  
    A dictionary that learns

    Teach your speech model your words.

    Local models such as Parakeet and Whisper.cpp are fast and keep your audio on your computer, but they can mishear names and jargon. Entune closes that gap with recordings you already have: it transcribes them with the model you dictate with, and builds a dictionary from the words that model gets wrong.

    
      
        01Bring your recordingsIn Dictionary, learn from recordings already in Entune, another dictation app on your Mac, or a folder. Only the audio is copied; the other app's transcripts are never read.

        02Pick the model you dictate withEntune transcribes the audio with it, so its own mistakes show up: a local model one recording at a time, a cloud model four at a time.

        03Find what it gets wrongA language model reads the transcripts in parts and suggests entries for that speech model, in the background while you keep dictating. Stop keeps finished parts for Continue.

        04Review, apply, dictateEdit any suggestion, leave out what you don't want, and apply the rest. When a word could mean either, your decision model then picks what the sentence means.

    Entries belong to the speech model they were learned on, because every model mishears differently. Pin an entry to use it with every model; suggestions can't remove pinned entries. Later runs can revise or remove learned entries, and you review each change.

  




  
    History you keep

    Every recording, on your disk, with what happened to it.

    Replay the audio. Copy the text. See what each processing step changed. Transcribe a recording again with another model and compare. Provider failures stay visible. Nothing is uploaded to Entune, because there is no Entune server.

    Privacy, said plainly

    No account. No telemetry. No hosted history.

    
      
        Speech. Cloud speech sends audio to the provider you chose. Local speech keeps it on your computer.

        Corrections and formatting. Off until you turn them on. Then your decision model reads the text: Jev sends it to TypeSafe, OpenAI's Decisions API to OpenAI, and Perplexity to Perplexity, even when speech is local. Laya keeps it on your computer.

        Your dictionary. Building it runs only when you ask, and sends the transcripts it reads, and the entries in them, to the language model you chose.

        Your files. Audio, transcripts, dictionary, settings and keys live in one folder. Settings › Data & privacy exports your audio and transcripts, or deletes everything.

        Use Entune on a computer only you use: its local API has no password, so other programs on it can read your recordings. Data and privacy, in full

      Questions

      Every answer, without the wall of text.

      Each topic opens to the detail you need, then links to the full guide. New to dictation? Start with what dictation software does.

    

    
      
        Is it really free?
        Yes. Entune is MIT licensed, with no Entune subscription. Local speech models run on your computer with no API key or per-minute payment. Cloud models use your own accounts and can cost money.
Choosing models →

      
      
        Does my audio leave my computer?
        Only if you choose cloud speech, and then only to the provider you picked. Local speech keeps it on your computer. There is no Entune server.
Dictate offline →

      
      
        What does the decision model actually do?
        When a dictionary match could mean your term or an everyday word, it reads the words around it and applies only the meaning that fits. It chooses from your own entries. It never generates or rewrites your text.
Decision-model results →

      
      
        Do I need an API key?
        Not for local speech. To build your dictionary, choose Sign in with ChatGPT and your plan's usage applies. Prefer a key? OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq and Mistral work too.
Correct names and technical terms →

      
      
        How long does building a dictionary take?
        It depends on how much you give it. In our October test, 7.5 hours of dictation took 39 minutes in 10 parts. Dictation keeps working throughout, and Stop keeps finished parts for Continue.
Dictionary reference →

      
      
        Which systems does it run on?
        macOS, Windows and Linux. macOS has been tested by hand; Windows and Linux are covered by automated tests. Linux is new, with shortcuts and paste on X11 and Wayland.
Using Entune →

      
      
        Can I dictate prompts to a coding agent?
        Yes. Entune pastes into the input you are in, such as an agent's chat box in your editor or a prompt in your browser, and your dictionary keeps library names and flags right. On a Mac, delivery into a terminal has been tested in Ghostty. There is a guide for Claude Code too.
Dictate to coding agents →

      
    

  




  
    
      Install

      One command. Then three steps.

      
        macOS
        Windows
        Linux
      

      
        $
        uv tool install entune && entune
        Copy
      

      Puts Entune in Applications and opens it. The first start can take up to a minute.Puts Entune in the Start menu and opens it, in Windows PowerShell.Puts Entune in your applications menu and opens it. Linux needs a few system libraries; see the Linux guide. Needs uv; without it, on Python 3.12 or newer: python -m pip install entune && entune

    

    
      
        01
        Set up a speech model

        In Models, paste a provider's API key or download a local model. The first one becomes your default. Parakeet, on Apple Silicon, first needs its engine: uv tool install parakeet-mlx.

      

      
        02
        Allow permissions

        On macOS: Microphone, Accessibility and Input Monitoring, each from its own button.On Windows, only the microphone.On Linux, keyboard access: one command, run once, then log out and back in.

      

      
        03
        Set a shortcut

        Hold it in any app and speak, or toggle hands-free recording. The text is pasted where you are, or copied if no text field is active.

      

    
    You can start without a dictionary or decision model and add them later. To upgrade: uv tool upgrade entune && entune
